rule: GOAL: Arrange four colored blocks in the middle box to match the specific color sequence displayed in the top row. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click an empty slot in the middle box to place it. RULE: The top row acts as the target pattern; the middle box must replicate this left-to-right order exactly. TRAP: Assuming the bottom palette’s initial arrangement is the solution wastes moves; you must reorder them to match the top reference.

GOAL: Move two colored plus-shapes so their arms cover specific target dots on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently active color; Space switches control between the two colors. RULE: Each plus has fixed arm lengths; you must position centers so arms intersect all assigned targets. TRAP: Assuming you can move shapes off-board to reach distant dots; movement stops at the grid edge.

GOAL: Guide the purple square along the dotted track to reach the ball. CONTROLS: Click a spot on the track to move the square to that position. RULE: The square can only move a limited distance along the path per click. TRAP: Assuming you can jump anywhere instantly; clicking too far away causes no movement.

GOAL: Move the yellow handle to the black wall’s gap. CONTROLS: Click the top blue block to extend the gray piston right; click the bottom blue block to retract it left. RULE: The piston only moves when the blue blocks are clicked, not the gray area itself. TRAP: Assuming the yellow handle moves vertically; it only shifts horizontally within its row band.

GOAL: Align the diamond ring to cover three red dots, then position the blue plus over the final target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; the spacebar switches control between the diamond and the blue plus. RULE: Red dots merge into the ring only when the diamond’s outline passes directly over them. TRAP: Assuming the diamond absorbs dots on contact; it must pass exactly over them to count as covered.

GOAL: The player had to guide a plug into a socket by moving it five spaces down. CONTROLS: Clicking bars or stems toggled their color, while pressing the central button executed the resulting movement commands. RULE: Black stems generated downward moves, allowing the piece to slide through clear columns into the waiting receptacle. TRAP: Believing bars controlled movement wasted time, as only the vertical stems dictated the direction of travel.

GOAL: Stop the magenta flood before it destroys the two castles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the shield paddle; Space activates a special action. RULE: Placing the paddle directly under the nozzle blocks the flow at the source. TRAP: You might think you need to catch the falling goo, but plugging the top hole is the only solution.

GOAL: Shift the key right into the open space. CONTROLS: Click blue blocks to slide the gray boundary; adjacent bands move opposite directions. RULE: A click only moves the boundary where no blue block blocks the path. TRAP: Assuming all rows in a band shift together; anchored rows resist movement due to obstacles.

GOAL: Place a crate on a marked square. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player and carried crate; space picks up or drops the crate. RULE: The crate moves with the player when carried, allowing precise positioning. TRAP: Believing the facing direction matters for dropping; it does not.

GOAL: Traverse the maze from the start corner to the exit corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell at a time between grid points. RULE: Movement is only possible between adjacent open cells; walls block passage entirely. TRAP: Believing you must jump over walls or move two spaces; simple single-step navigation works.

GOAL: Rotate five stacked glyphs to match a target sequence using limited moves. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the selection cursor; up and down arrows rotate the selected glyph. RULE: Each glyph cycles through a fixed set of six shapes, so aligning one column never disturbs the others. TRAP: Assuming you must press down to rotate; pressing up is often shorter if the cycle wraps around.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks into their matching target boxes to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click a block to hold it; click another slot to swap their positions; press Space to submit. RULE: The game only accepts the solution when every block sits in the box matching its specific color. TRAP: Assuming you can carry a block without swapping it away from its original spot wastes moves and confuses the state.

GOAL: Cover all dots simultaneously using three rotating shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles to the next one. RULE: Dots vanish only while covered but reappear once the shape moves away. TRAP: Assuming dots stay hidden permanently; they must all be under a shape at the exact same moment.

GOAL: Place colored blocks into specific slots within color-coded boxes to form a continuous sequence. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette, then click a gray slot in a box to place it. Press Space to submit the arrangement. RULE: Insert each box’s blocks into the main sequence exactly at the pipe location matching that box’s color. TRAP: Assuming all boxes insert at the first pipe, rather than their specific color-matched pipe positions.

GOAL: Align five rotating glyph slots to match the target pattern above. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move the selection cursor; Up arrow rotates the active slot forward. RULE: All slots share one cyclic order, so learning the sequence on one slot helps solve the others. TRAP: Assuming each slot has a unique cycle forces inefficient brute-force searching instead of using the shared order.

GOAL: Align liquid surfaces just below gaps so floating keys block the flow. CONTROLS: Click pumps to transfer liquid between connected tanks. RULE: Keys ride the liquid surface; they seal gaps only when perfectly aligned. TRAP: Assuming liquid fills to the very top; overfilling causes overflow instead of sealing.

GOAL: Route the color sequence through a split path using a pipe. CONTROLS: Click slots to grab items; click targets to place; press space to verify. RULE: Placing the N ring turns a red slot into a conduit, splicing the green box’s items into the main reading order. TRAP: Assuming pipes are fixed scenery; here, you must manually place the ring to bridge the disconnected green section.

ESTABLISHED: The arm extends in six-unit steps from a retracted position, with its tip reaching the right edge after five presses. FAILED: Pressing left while the arm hooks a block resulted in no movement, likely due to collision or clamping. GOAL IS NOT: The objective is not to simply align the arm with the block at the right edge. CONTROLS: Vertical movement shifts the arm's row alignment, while horizontal presses extend or retract the arm in fixed increments.

GOAL: Pass a stationary blocker to reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step. RULE: The blocker only lunges if you are in the same row within two steps at the turn start. TRAP: Believing the blocker attacks from any direction. It ignores you in adjacent rows, letting you slip past safely.

GOAL: Match shape colors to dot colors by painting them on corresponding squares. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches which shape is active. RULE: Paint is permanent; a shape keeps its new color even after leaving the square. TRAP: Thinking you must cover dots with a shape’s original color; you must recolor them first.

GOAL: Arrange solids and conduits to match a hidden sequence, ensuring shared blue rings align with red slots. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, then click grid slots to place. Press space to verify and solve. RULE: Blue conduits must occupy red slots that correspond to identical positions in the sequence. TRAP: Assuming blue order was arbitrary; left-to-right alignment of shared rings was critical for the solution.

GOAL: Route three colored rings through a central box to link external boxes, matching the top sequence's color triples. CONTROLS: Click palette items to place rings in the center and solids in outer slots; press space to submit. RULE: Each center ring determines which external box fills the next three sequence slots, starting with that box's fixed color. TRAP: Assuming rings just decorate the center; they actually act as connectors defining which box contributes to which sequence segment.

GOAL: Merge two M tokens into P, then P with another P to form Y, and push Y onto the ball. CONTROLS: Clicks moved tokens five spaces in the clicked direction; clicking between two tokens of the same type merged them. RULE: Merged tokens grow larger and change color, requiring precise positioning to align their edges for the next merge. TRAP: Assuming all moves are orthogonal; diagonal clicks were necessary to align the growing squares correctly for merging.

GOAL: Match each slot’s glyph to the correct pair’s output by rotating it into the target shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys cycle the current slot’s glyph through its rotation states. RULE: A slot is solved only when its glyph matches the target’s exact orientation, not just its shape. TRAP: Assuming rotational symmetry means any rotation fits; some pairs require a specific, non-symmetric angle.

GOAL: Navigate from start to goal while consuming three stationary guards that block specific rows and columns. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell in the selected direction; moving into a guard consumes it. RULE: Guards are static and only dangerous if the player occupies a cell within their fixed line of sight. TRAP: Assuming guards move or track the player causes hesitation; they remain fixed, so timing relative to their position matters less than simple line-of-sight avoidance.

GOAL: Transform the initial shape through a hidden two-stage chain to produce the final yellow pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selection cursor; Up rotated the current wheel; Down was a backup rotation method. RULE: Each input shape mapped to a pink intermediate, which then uniquely determined the yellow output shape. TRAP: Assuming the wheel rotation direction was fixed caused wasted time; some slots required counter-intuitive turns to match targets.

GOAL: Grow two bars to touch their target plus signs. CONTROLS: Click left piece to extend red bar down; click right piece to extend green bar right. RULE: The small red dot trails the bar tip and must land exactly on the plus center. TRAP: Overlapping the bar with the plus does not win; only the trailing dot touching the center counts.

GOAL: Reach the white sparkle marker to clear the room. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your block five cells per press. RULE: Walls block movement, so plan paths around obstacles before moving. TRAP: Assume the top frame is the exit; ignore it and seek the sparkle.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align colors at the arrow entry points. CONTROLS: Click arrows to spin the ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: The level completes when the colors at both arrow slots match. TRAP: Assuming the yellow brackets marked a target location; they were just empty space indicators.

GOAL: Shrink a block to fit a narrow channel and slide it into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicking diamond cells toggles its size. RULE: The block shrinks from the right edge, allowing it to enter tight spaces. TRAP: Assuming the block shrinks symmetrically or from the left wastes moves trying to align it incorrectly.

GOAL: Make the fourth grid match its small mirror pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a big tile toggles its color. RULE: The mini-grid shows the target; the big grid must match it exactly. TRAP: Thinking the mini-grid was just a cursor; it is actually the goal state.

GOAL: Shrink the block to fit through the narrow vertical channel and plug it into the top socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; keypad cells trigger transmissions that change block size. RULE: Each transmission toggles the block between full and small sizes, regardless of pattern count. TRAP: Assuming pattern size dictates block size; it only toggles state, so check current size before moving.

GOAL: Match the 5x3 grid to the two overlapping reference blocks. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between blue and orange. RULE: The overlapping middle row must satisfy the pattern of both reference blocks simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming the two reference blocks operate independently; they share row two, forcing a strict consistency check.

GOAL: Place the square precisely on the ring. CONTROLS: Click empty space to teleport; click the gray diamond to swap positions. RULE: The square lands on the midpoint between the white and gray markers. TRAP: Assuming the gray diamond is a fixed obstacle rather than a swappable anchor.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over neighbors into empty spaces. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a destination to jump. RULE: A peg can only jump if it lands on an empty spot immediately beyond an adjacent peg. TRAP: Clicking empty cells does nothing; you must click the peg itself to start a move.

GOAL: Paint every tile red or orange to match the hidden pattern shown by the mini-grids. CONTROLS: Click a tile to cycle its color; observe the small grids to determine which color each cell should become. RULE: The dot color in a mini-grid tells you what white tiles become; gray tiles always become the opposite color. TRAP: Assuming gray tiles match the dot color; they actually map to the non-dot color, causing repeated mismatches at overlapping zones.

GOAL: Place both yellow tokens onto the two target brackets to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click buttons to rotate specific rings of cells, shifting tokens along their paths. RULE: The yellow tokens are identical; only the final arrangement on the target cells matters, not which token lands where. TRAP: Assuming the two rings operate independently; they actually share perimeter cells, so rotating one ring shifts tokens that belong to the other.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow and orange regions are separated by a central channel; blocks are inside the arch wall. FAILED: Making blocks adjacent at (1,5) and (1,6) did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simple adjacency between the two blocks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously in the same direction; moves are blocked by walls.

GOAL: Grow the green shape to reach the far right target. CONTROLS: Click edges to expand or shrink shapes; movement pushes connected pieces. RULE: Shrinking one piece pulls the whole chain, clearing space for later growth. TRAP: Growing green early blocks the path; shrink yellow and green first to shift the cluster right.

GOAL: Place the yellow block in the yellow bracket and the orange block in the orange bracket. CONTROLS: Clicking a colored button rotates the ring, moving all blocks along the path in that direction. RULE: Blocks follow the ring's path; they cannot jump gaps or pass through each other. TRAP: Assuming blocks swap positions directly; they actually slide along the track, requiring precise rotation counts to align them.

GOAL: Match the board to the target pattern using 19 clicks. CONTROLS: Click tiles to cycle colors blue to red to orange. RULE: Mini-dots pair with the opposite color, forcing gray cells to change. TRAP: Assuming gray cells stay static wastes clicks; they must match the paired color.

ESTABLISHED: Moving the active square directly into the ring does not clear the level. FAILED: Placing the active square in the ring. GOAL IS NOT: Simply having the active square occupy the ring location. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active square; clicking selects the active square.

ESTABLISHED: You are a block. A red blob travels along a wire. A ghost replays your previous path. The exit is at the bottom right. FAILED: Pressing UP at the start was a no-op and did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not to collide with the ghost or the red blob. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your block. The ghost and red blob move independently on their own paths.

GOAL: Move both blocks to the bottom corners. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; switch active blocks to navigate. RULE: Blocks cannot pass through each other in narrow lanes; use open spaces to swap positions. TRAP: Assuming blocks can cross paths at the top center; they must pass around each other in the wide base.

GOAL: Guide a square into the hidden target socket. CONTROLS: Click to select a square; arrows move the selected piece. RULE: Only the active square moves; unselected squares slide until blocked by walls. TRAP: Assuming the pushed square was the goal; the stationary square was actually the key.

GOAL: Arrange solid blocks and connector rings so the yellow block lands in the fourth position. CONTROLS: Drag solids to slots and rings to connector points, then press Space to test the sequence. RULE: Rings splice entire nested boxes into the parent slot, expanding the list and shifting positions. TRAP: Assuming rings are just placeholders; they actually insert a whole sub-sequence, changing the total count.

GOAL: Align the plug’s prongs with the socket holes so the body avoids the green zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug; Space rotates it ninety degrees clockwise. RULE: Success requires prongs to face right, entering holes from the left without body overlap. TRAP: Believing any orientation fitting the holes wins; wrong rotation caused body collisions.

GOAL: Guide the shape to the matching yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; the dotted ghost mirrors it instantly. RULE: You only control one piece; the reflection always copies your moves. TRAP: Thinking both shapes were independent led to wasted time trying to steer the ghost.

GOAL: Move the block to the exit while the ghost travels a fixed path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; the ghost moves automatically each turn. RULE: Sharing a cell is safe; only leaving a cell the ghost still occupies causes failure. TRAP: Believing overlapping cells are always deadly, causing unnecessary detours instead of using direct paths.

GOAL: Move the charcoal block onto the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space switches between linked pieces. RULE: One piece moves directly; the other shifts inversely to maintain spacing. TRAP: Assuming both pieces move independently ignores the linked inverse shift.

GOAL: Guide the green knob from the start to the target slot by navigating through shifting barriers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the knob; clicking colored blocks toggles their orientation to open or close paths. RULE: Only the block matching the knob's current color can be clicked to change the maze layout. TRAP: Assuming a path stays open; clicking a block shifts it, potentially blocking your exit if you don't re-evaluate the route immediately.

GOAL: Fit four distinct blocks into their matching socket rings on the board. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the currently selected block one step in that direction. Clicks selected a specific block to make it active for movement. RULE: Only the selected block moves; others stay fixed until clicked. TRAP: Assuming all blocks could move simultaneously or that clicking moved the block rather than just selecting it.

GOAL: Clear Level 5 in exactly eight moves using only directional inputs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; Spacebar cycles between cursor shapes. RULE: The cursor paints only when its shape matches the target color. TRAP: Assuming a complex path was needed; the solution was a simple straight line.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while managing ghost paths. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player block. RULE: Ghosts replay absolute recorded paths; one successful move advances all active ghosts by one step. TRAP: Assuming ghosts reset relative to the player; they follow fixed global coordinates, requiring precise move counting to clear gates.

GOAL: Rotate the cup to face the canvas and pour paint to fill the target area. CONTROLS: Click to select paint; Space to pour; Arrow keys to rotate the cup's orientation. RULE: The cup's opening must align directly with the canvas to deposit paint correctly. TRAP: Assuming the visual tilt matches the pour direction; the opening always faces the canvas center regardless of rotation.

GOAL: Touch the pink plus symbol to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character in grid steps. RULE: Walking directly into the target object triggers the win condition. TRAP: Assuming the black outline acts as a solid wall blocking your path.

GOAL: Rearrange the grid tiles into the target pattern using the fewest clicks possible. CONTROLS: Click red arrows to shift rows or columns forward; click green arrows to shift them backward. RULE: Red and green arrows on the same axis are exact inverses, allowing precise undoing of moves. TRAP: Assuming symmetry allows skipping verification led to wasted actions when a specific axis behaved unexpectedly.

GOAL: Align the green plug and blue U to their holes so all red pins turn gray. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; clicks select a different object. RULE: Objects only connect when pins perfectly overlap holes, turning them gray. TRAP: Assuming holes stay red; connected holes turn gray, making them invisible if you only look for red.

GOAL: Align a movable mirror so reflected shapes match the yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; Space cycles selection between pieces and the mirror. RULE: Reflections flip vertically across the mirror’s center line, preserving horizontal position. TRAP: Believing pieces must be moved to match targets; instead, only the mirror needs vertical adjustment to catch the reflections.

GOAL: Paint the top half purple and the bottom-right triangle orange. CONTROLS: Arrows roll the ink cup; clicks select colors; space pours ink. RULE: Each direction masks a specific half-plane of the grid. TRAP: Pouring purple from the northwest corner wrongly colors the white bottom-left corner.

GOAL: Move the two yellow blocks to the marked corners of the top row. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows rotate the top row or the entire serpentine path. RULE: The large arrow moves every block along the winding path; the small arrow spins only the top row. TRAP: Assuming the large arrow moves blocks randomly; it actually shifts them in a strict, unbroken line.

GOAL: Move two distinct tokens into their respective target zones. CONTROLS: Click near a token to pull it closer; click far away to push it. RULE: Tokens move toward the click if within range, otherwise they stay put. TRAP: Assuming tokens vanish upon touching a target; they remain until all objectives are met.

GOAL: Merge two distinct shapes to form a single, continuous block that perfectly covers the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; the spacebar cycles selection to the next available piece. RULE: A piece is only "absorbed" when it completely overlaps a colored region, leaving no gaps. TRAP: Believing you must move each piece to its final spot individually; sometimes overlapping them creates the required shape faster.

GOAL: Match six rotating glyphs to the sky pattern using a limited action budget. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP and DOWN rotate the selected glyph. RULE: The cursor wraps around, so taking the shortest path between boxes saves actions. TRAP: Assuming UP is always faster wastes turns; check if DOWN reaches the target sooner.

GOAL: Route the electrical signal from the keypad to the correct blue socket. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the central plug; other keys toggle power flow through connected pipes. RULE: Signals always travel along the longest continuous open path away from the source. TRAP: Assuming signals seek the nearest socket; they instead follow the most extended available track.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the exit while managing a strict movement budget. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; each action drains energy. RULE: Energy depletes rapidly, forcing a direct, efficient path to the goal. TRAP: Assuming safe zones allow wandering; lingering quickly drains energy to zero.

GOAL: Rotate the cross to open the path, plug the channel, and push the dark red band to the target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks on colored buttons rotate arms or plug channels. RULE: The cross orientation dictates which arm allows passage, requiring precise timing of rotation clicks. TRAP: Assuming the bar drains evenly per step led to wasted moves; it ticks slower than actions.

GOAL: Cover all yellow cells using the piece and its reflections. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection between walls and the piece. RULE: Moving a reflection wall shifts the mirror line, changing where the piece’s reflections appear. TRAP: Assuming the piece moves directly; you must move the invisible wall to position the reflection.

GOAL: Move three yellow blocks into bracketed slots and close the bridge. CONTROLS: Click spokes or rings to rotate parts; click the bridge to swap positions. RULE: Rotations in separate regions do not interfere, allowing independent planning for each block. TRAP: Assuming the bridge can be used to navigate blocks to their slots; it only swaps final positions.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while dodging moving obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step per press. RULE: Obstacles follow fixed, repeating paths; time your moves to slip through gaps. TRAP: Assuming obstacles move randomly wastes time; they are predictable, so observe their cycles first.

GOAL: Move two yellow pieces into their target slots by rotating two rings and swapping a trio. CONTROLS: Red button rotates the large and center rings. Green button swaps three small cells. RULE: Each red click rotates both rings simultaneously, forcing you to park pieces in the swap zone to avoid unwanted movement. TRAP: Believing you must move each yellow piece independently; ignoring the shared rotation cycle wastes moves on back-and-forth corrections.

GOAL: Match liquid heights on both sides of a barrier to unlock a passage for a floating key. CONTROLS: Clicking blue zones pumps liquid between adjacent columns; clicking an activated plug moves the key across. RULE: The barrier only opens when the liquid levels on both sides are exactly equal. TRAP: Believing any height difference allows passage wastes time; precise alignment is required before the plug turns orange.

GOAL: Slide the large shape left and up to uncover the hidden piece and align their dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; clicking selects the topmost shape. RULE: Only the top shape is clickable; you must move blockers to reveal buried pieces. TRAP: Assuming covered shapes can be selected directly; they are inaccessible until the top shape moves away.

GOAL: Position the central bar and side blocks to match the reflection pattern while clearing the path. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected pieces; clicking selects a piece; walls slide along their axis. RULE: Pieces must align with their mirror images across the central axis to lock in place. TRAP: Assuming walls move freely like blocks; they only slide along their fixed orientation, requiring precise selection before moving.

GOAL: Move the pegs from panels A and C into the carrier and return home. CONTROLS: Click cells to move the carrier along the track; click the carrier to select it for jumps. RULE: The carrier must physically visit each panel to collect its pegs before returning to the start. TRAP: Believing emptying the first panel ends the level; the carrier must still retrieve the second panel’s pegs.

GOAL: Position the handle so its calculated midpoint aligns with the target ring. CONTROLS: Click a grid square to move the handle there; click another piece to swap positions. RULE: The handle snaps to a target only when the average of its current and anchor coordinates matches the target center. TRAP: Assuming any close click triggers a snap; you must precisely calculate the required anchor position first.

GOAL: Paint the grid into four colored zones matching the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the nozzle; clicks select colors or trigger pours. RULE: Each pour fills the current directional quadrant, overwriting previous colors in that area. TRAP: Assuming rotations persist between turns; you must re-orient the nozzle before every single pour.

GOAL: Fill four quadrants and spray a hidden corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the bottle; mouse clicks select paint or trigger the nozzle. RULE: Squirt coverage depends entirely on the bottle’s current rotation angle. TRAP: Assuming the nozzle stays fixed; it moves with the bottle, so you must rotate to W before spraying yellow.

GOAL: Move the green and blue tokens into their matching colored zones. CONTROLS: Click pumps to raise liquid levels; click plugs to release liquid and open gates. RULE: A plug only opens when the liquid level exactly matches its required height. TRAP: Clicking a pump repeatedly raises the level too high, overshooting the precise height needed to open the gate.

GOAL: Move the frame to the target, then guide the plus shape to its dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches between the frame and the plus. RULE: Only the active shape responds to arrows; the other stays fixed until switched. TRAP: Assuming arrows move both shapes simultaneously wastes moves; switch to the plus before navigating its path.

GOAL: Grow the small plug to fit the large socket and slide it in. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; plus grows it toward the blue side and down. RULE: Growth extends the blue-facing edge by two cells and adds depth downward. TRAP: Trying to move a large plug into the socket fails; it must grow in place.

GOAL: Navigate the maze to collect all six red nodes and reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one grid step in the chosen direction. RULE: Obstacles follow a strict, repeating movement pattern, requiring precise timing to pass. TRAP: Assuming obstacles remain stationary or move randomly leads to collisions; they cycle predictably.

GOAL: Align the T piece’s red ends with the S and K pieces to complete all four color pairs. CONTROLS: Click the piece body to select, then use arrows to move. RULE: Red blocks must touch matching red blocks to form a gray connection. TRAP: Assuming K’s red block is at its visual center; it is actually at the corner.

GOAL: Guide the green block to push two cross shapes into their matching floor sockets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green block; it pushes adjacent blocks in the direction of movement. RULE: Blocks slide continuously until hitting a wall or another block, making precise stopping points impossible. TRAP: Believing you can stop a block mid-slide; you must use obstacles to halt them exactly at the target.

GOAL: Fill the canvas by rotating the nozzle to align with the target paint color and clicking to pour. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the nozzle orientation; mouse clicks select paint or trigger the pour action. RULE: The nozzle must face the exact direction of the paint source to draw liquid; misalignment yields nothing. TRAP: Assuming clicks work without first rotating the nozzle to the correct facing, wasting turns on empty pours.

GOAL: Move the key to the right zone by managing fluid levels. CONTROLS: Click tanks to transfer liquid between adjacent sections; click plugs to move the key. RULE: The key’s position depends on the fluid surface height, so match levels to align with plug openings. TRAP: Assuming plugs open automatically wastes time; you must click them manually even when levels look correct.

ESTABLISHED: Four green anchors form a fixed set; moving the purple handle swaps its position with a purple gray spot without altering the green set. FAILED: Clicking water squares causes no changes and halts execution; incorrect centroid calculations lead to invalid targets. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing pieces anywhere; the centroid of specific anchor groups must match exact ring centers while maintaining minimum distances. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell moves the active handle; clicking a gray spot swaps it with the handle; clicks on invalid squares are rejected.

GOAL: Move the left block across the center line to the right side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the connected pair one cell in that direction. RULE: The level ends only when the blocks move right, not left. TRAP: Assuming the puzzle is symmetrical; moving left does not count as crossing.

ESTABLISHED: The counter tracks actions per level and resets to zero upon restart. Two carriers exist, one loaded. Movement is reversible without immediate failure. FAILED: Moving carrier 2 to reveal the map to the right and down did not trigger a clear. GOAL IS NOT: Surviving a strict step limit, as the counter does not cause death. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active carrier; mouse clicks reset the level and zero the counter.

GOAL: Align three floating shapes with a fixed anchor to connect seven red ports. CONTROLS: Arrows moved pieces, Space rotated them, clicks selected targets. RULE: Shapes only snap when red ports perfectly overlap, turning gray to confirm. TRAP: Assuming rotation kept the center fixed; it shifted the pivot, forcing extra moves to realign the origin.

GOAL: Move the linked pair to the target zone using one click. CONTROLS: Click a valid land spot to shift the pair’s center toward it. RULE: The handle anchors the movement; the center moves exactly half the distance between the old and new handle positions. TRAP: Ignoring the parity rule. If the new handle position creates a fractional center coordinate, the move is invalid, wasting your only click.

ESTROLISHED: The left panel is dimmed and inactive; the right panel accepts mixed-column programs sequentially. A T-piece at row 2 moves the plug up three spaces. FAILED: Attempting to activate left panel toggles or cards produced no movement; the plug did not move up when testing other row configurations. GOAL IS NOT: The left panel is not the active control zone, nor are the cards independent movement rules for the right panel. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells places program pieces; pressing run executes the sequence left-to-right, top-to-bottom, moving the plug accordingly.

GOAL: Move walls and pieces to cover yellow zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected objects; click selects. RULE: Reflections absorb yellow when aligned with targets. TRAP: Believing walls stay static; they must be repositioned to trigger reflections.

ESTABLISHED: Gray mini glyphs W/g map to dot rules. Magenta minis encode M→dot, N→other. Current board fails win condition. Clicking minis yields no change. FAILED: T1 target pattern. T2 minus one tile. Interpreting g as base color. Assuming gray glyphs are literal colors. Clicking purple/green HUD swatches. GOAL IS NOT: Making every mini’s block contain purple. Making blocks non-monochrome. Matching literal gray/white tiles. Satisfying dot rules alone. CONTROLS: Clicking tiles paints. Clicking minis is inert. Clicking HUD swatches is inert.

ESTABLISHED: The magenta podium swaps the green and magenta knobs' positions. Absorbing the purple key triggers the purple podium. FAILED: Moving the knob away from the isolated island before absorbing the key. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the isolated island; the key must be absorbed there. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the knob; clicking a podium places a colored plug into the corresponding channel.

ESTABLISHED: The paddle reaches rows sixteen to nineteen. The fail pattern shows a top bar and flashing cups. FAILED: Pouring with the paddle at rows twenty to twenty-three, twenty-four to twenty-seven, and twenty-eight to thirty-one produced only the fail pattern. GOAL IS NOT: Filling a single cup. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the paddle. The space bar pours the liquid.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking blocks converts them to water; the player floats up and moves left across liquid surfaces. FAILED: Moving right or staying still yields no progress; single-side water contact does not trigger melting. GOAL IS NOT: Simple navigation; the objective is not merely reaching a coordinate but triggering a specific room transition via vertical rise. CONTROLS: Click blocks to melt them. Arrow keys move the player. Rising to the water's surface triggers a shuffle.

GOAL: Guide two linked blocks to a collision point. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Mirrored movement means one block moves opposite to the other, allowing them to pass through each other. TRAP: Treating them as a single unit; they are two distinct entities with linked, opposite controls.

GOAL: Move the knob from the starting box to the yellow target by navigating a grid blocked by rotating cross-shaped obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the knob; clicking a colored podium rotates that specific cross structure. RULE: The knob can only pass through a cross’s arms if the cross is rotated to align with the path; otherwise, it is blocked. TRAP: Believing the knob could slip through the gap between two different crosses without first rotating the blocking cross into the correct orientation.

ESTABLISHED: Three boxes remain unplaced; step bar shows thirty-six. Orange activates one box at a time but can trigger adjacent boxes simultaneously if positioned correctly. FAILED: Moving box D to standard holding spots created blocking paths for box C. Sequential manual deliveries consumed too many steps. GOAL IS NOT: Placing boxes in fixed starting positions. The container accepts boxes from various angles if unblocked. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. Touching the orange activates nearby boxes to slide toward the goal.

ESTABLISHED: Walls cannot push other walls or immovable blocks. Bars have fixed roots and cannot be displaced by growing shapes. FAILED: Attempting to shrink the red wall to displace the vertical wall. Trying to shrink the orange wall to move the blue block. GOAL IS NOT: A solution relying on pushing stacked walls or moving fixed bars into place. CONTROLS: Shrinking and growing walls are blocked if the destination overlaps any existing wall or block.

ESTABLISHED: You are at the socket. The plus, ring, and socket locations are unique and fixed. FAILED: The previous route exhausted the budget without clearing. GOAL IS NOT: A single-pass run; you likely need to revisit stations to refill energy. CONTROLS: Moving costs energy. Stepping on rings refills the bar. This refill is repeatable, allowing multiple trips between points.

GOAL: Move the block to the blue ring using exactly three actions. CONTROLS: Click anchors to lift or swap; drag to position the block. RULE: Each move must keep the block’s footprint clear of static obstacles and voids. TRAP: Assuming the bottom-left void extends to the edge; the jagged border leaves safe cells nearby.

ESTABLISHED: The cross pushes freely up to rows 14-22, overlapping the ring's border without stopping or triggering a win. FAILED: Pushing the cross further up from its current position to reach the ring's center. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing the cross to the top edge or overlapping the ring's border cells. CONTROLS: Green pieces push the cross when moving into its lower notches; the cross moves one tile per push until blocked.

ESTABLISHED: The bar is a hard budget; zero means death. The goal area is disconnected by walls. The chaser stays in the left region and never breaks barriers. FAILED: Trying to reach the right side. Waiting for the chaser to break walls. Moving both characters as if co-op. Hiding in dead ends. GOAL IS NOT: Surviving until the bar empties. Reaching the isolated right-side cell. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue character. The bar drops by two per step. The chaser moves toward blue but stops at walls.

ESTABLISHED: Tokens merge and move toward clicks. The pursuer always targets the nearest token. Merging reduces total token count. FAILED: Moving tokens in parallel while being chased leads to elimination. Attempting to outrun the pursuer directly fails. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the exit or avoiding the pursuer forever. CONTROLS: Click empty spaces to move tokens. Click tokens to merge them. Tokens move one step per click.

GOAL: Move two blocks to meet at a central marker. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; clicks select a block or the marker. RULE: Selecting a block makes it active; selecting the marker moves it alone. TRAP: Assuming arrow keys move all objects simultaneously when one is selected.

ESTABLISHED: The blue box with the dot is the goal. White areas are walls, not walkable rooms. The start cell has no box. FAILED: Moving into white cells does nothing. Pressing the emitter toggles the yellow block but does not open paths or move the block into the goal. GOAL IS NOT: The start cell. The emitter itself. The yellow block's home position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. Pressing the emitter toggles the yellow block's state or position, but it does not currently interact with the goal or gates effectively.

GOAL: Move the white handle to absorb the hidden token while maintaining the centroid balance. CONTROLS: Click the handle to move it to a new anchor position; the system automatically adjusts the invisible mass to keep the sum constant. RULE: The average position of all anchors must always equal the fixed target centroid, regardless of individual moves. TRAP: Believing the handle moves independently; it is constrained by the total sum, so every move requires a pre-calculated counter-weight to avoid invalid states.

GOAL: Traverse the maze from start to finish, collecting the key and reaching the exit before the chaser catches you. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in that direction. RULE: The chaser always moves one step toward your current position after you move. TRAP: Assuming you can outrun the chaser in open corridors; you must use the layout to break line-of-sight or force detours.

GOAL: Reach the yellow exit by navigating a moving knob through shifting platforms. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicking colors shifts specific platform bars. RULE: Clicking a color moves that bar’s position, allowing you to extend tracks for the knob. TRAP: Assuming gray clicks are for movement; they only reset the bottom track’s openness.

ESTABLISHED: A gray wall with a cross-shaped hole blocks the path. Bars move freely along their length but are blocked by the wall when moving perpendicular. FAILED: Pushing bars straight through the wall; moving the horizontal bar vertically; attempting to bypass the wall without alignment. GOAL IS NOT: Simply sliding bars into the hole without considering the wall's solid gray structure surrounding the passable channel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected bar. Movement is blocked if the bar hits the gray wall material.

GOAL: Seat the cross and two greens into their matching holes. CONTROLS: Arrows step the active piece one cell; clicks select a new piece. RULE: Rings block sliding moves but allow single-step walking onto their cells. TRAP: Thinking ring walls are solid everywhere; you can walk through them, but not slide through.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while avoiding the rival character. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; the rival moves automatically after every player step. RULE: When the rival has multiple valid moves, it prioritizes the cell the player visited most recently. TRAP: Assuming the rival uses fixed directional priority or follows the player’s immediate previous position leads to fatal misprediction.

GOAL: Seat the knob into the socket to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob across the grid. RULE: The knob must physically enter the socket’s hole to win. TRAP: Thinking the colored strips needed to fill the hole first; they were just background decoration.

GOAL: Guide two characters to meet at the seam between rooms. CONTROLS: Arrows move both characters simultaneously; walls block movement. RULE: Characters must end up adjacent or overlapping to trigger the exit. TRAP: Thinking one character stays on the pressure plate; you must move off it to approach the seam.

GOAL: Guide boxes to the container while dodging a sliding orange hazard. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; boxes slide until hitting a wall or other box. RULE: The orange activates on proximity, pushing boxes toward the goal along clear paths. TRAP: Assuming you must push every box personally; waiting for the orange to push one saved turns.

GOAL: Grow bars until their tips cover the center of each plus symbol. CONTROLS: Click the green panel boxes to extend the sky and pink bars. RULE: A bar is complete only when its tip covers the plus's center, not just its outer ring. TRAP: Stopping once the tip touches the plus's edge; the center cell must be covered for the level to finish.

GOAL: Slide the outer blocks inward until they hook onto the innermost block, matching the target arrangement. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the entire row left or right, but the innermost block stays pinned at the edge. RULE: Only blocks overlapping the previous position move; the rest stay put, creating a chain reaction. TRAP: Assuming all blocks in the lane move together fails when gaps exist, causing misalignment.

GOAL: Move blue balls to the yellow goal using limited clicks. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move nearest magnet; click two magnets to merge them. RULE: Merged magnets attract the ball strongly enough to pull it across gaps. TRAP: Believing you must click the ball itself; clicking magnets or empty space moves them.

ESTABLISHED: The claw grips the bottom bar; dragging it right opens a path. The purple ghost is currently pass-through. FAILED: Moving the claw to empty spots to release the bar. Clicking the ghost directly did not solidify it. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the knob to the track without bridging the gap or activating the ghost. CONTROLS: Drag the bar to fill gaps. Click the ghost region to toggle solidity. Guide the knob along the open path.

GOAL: Place the box in the container by timing its slide with the orange’s movement. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space picks up or drops the box. RULE: The box only slides when activated by the orange’s proximity, then follows its path. TRAP: Assuming the box moves immediately upon placement; it waits for the orange to trigger it.

ESTABLISHED: The plug moves only within its plus; black gaps block it. The keypad fires on the middle column and plus patterns, but arms on the Z. FAILED: Clicking the plug with the X pattern armed flashed the keypad red. GOAL IS NOT: The X pattern is not a valid firing sequence. CONTROLS: Keypad clicks arm or fire patterns based on shape; clicking the plug attempts to execute armed patterns.

ESTABLISHED: The plus is a static background marker; yellow bars cannot push it. The dot reaches only row 13 at best, while the plus center sits at row 10, making direct contact impossible. FAILED: Covering the plus with yellow segments does not trigger a win. Shrinking yellow to expose the center does not help. The dot landing on the center remains unachievable. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the dot directly on the plus center. Covering the plus shape with yellow color. CONTROLS: Yellow bars expand or shrink vertically. The dot moves horizontally. No control moves the plus or the dot vertically.

GOAL: Fill containers by guiding boxes to targets using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character to push or pull boxes. RULE: Boxes follow the player's path until they reach a valid container. TRAP: Assuming boxes slide indefinitely; they stop at walls or other boxes, requiring precise pathing to avoid blockages.

GOAL: Move the block into the box to cover the hidden glyph. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push the block one space in that direction. RULE: The block fits perfectly inside the box, triggering a win when fully enclosed. TRAP: Thinking the block must stay visible; it vanishes into the box upon success.

ESTABLISHED: Four blocks must be separated into distinct rows to prevent merging during travel. FAILED: Moving blocks together or leaving them in the player's row causes unwanted shoving or merging. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing all blocks to the right or clearing the board immediately. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; blocks slide until hitting walls or other blocks; the hand follows the player.

GOAL: Clear the level using nine actions. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle states; press button to execute pattern. RULE: Only specific shape combinations trigger the required movement. TRAP: Believing the action bar meant immediate death on last pixel; it allowed final execution.

GOAL: Guide the plug through the wall’s gap to the arch. CONTROLS: Click column slots to set stem or bar positions, then run the sequence. RULE: The plug follows the path defined by the assembled instructions step by step. TRAP: Assuming unverified card patterns move two cells when only single steps are confirmed.

GOAL: Match the blue glyph by rotating the starting shape 180 degrees. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; touching stations rotates the shape or changes the legend's color. RULE: Covering the mystery object sets the legend to blue, matching the target glyph's color. TRAP: The mystery object is not consumed when covered, so you can use it as a reusable color key.

ESTABLISHED: Chasers dash to clicks within 13 units, otherwise chase nearest movers. Movers must reach row 16 or higher to be safe from chasers blocked at row 20. Idle movers are bitten if a chaser ends adjacent. FAILED: Leaving movers idle near chasers. Failing to force movers upward before chasers close the gap. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clicking near movers. CONTROLS: Clicking moves chasers. If a click is within 13 units of a chaser, it dashes there; otherwise, it chases the closest mover.

GOAL: Trap the red block in a corner where it cannot escape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the paddle; clicking swaps the paddle with the target block. RULE: Only specific wide placements block all exit paths, requiring precise alignment. TRAP: Believing you must move the red block directly; instead, swap positions to reposition the paddle for the final drop.

ESTABLISHED: Five pieces have sixteen red prongs needing eight pairings. Four are currently linked. A yellow snake grows when eating white pellets near the clicked areas. FAILED: Clicking near the snake caused it to extend, blocking space without solving the puzzle. GOAL IS NOT: Feeding the snake or clearing the white pellets. CONTROLS: Clicking moves individual pieces to align red prongs into pairs while keeping bodies within bounds and away from the snake.

ESTROLISHED: The player holds a box attached to their right side. The target cell (7,2) is empty and accessible. The orange enemy is nearby in row 10 but does not currently block the planned northward path. FAILED: Previous attempts to clear the level failed to account for the enemy’s proximity, risking collision or path obstruction during movement. GOAL IS NOT: The objective is not to defeat the enemy or simply reach the target cell empty-handed; the box must be placed there. CONTROLS: UP moves north; LEFT moves west; SPACE drops the attached box at the current position.

GOAL: Match the tile grid and mini dots to the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click tiles to flip single colors; click minis to flip four adjacent tiles and toggle their own dot. RULE: Mini clicks only affect the four orthogonal neighbors, leaving the mini’s own cell and distant tiles unchanged. TRAP: Assuming mini clicks set neighbors to a fixed color instead of flipping them wastes time testing mixed states.

GOAL: Align the horizontal and vertical bars to cover the target pattern without touching the pools. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the bars along their respective axes to adjust their positions. RULE: Decorative frames do not block movement, allowing bars to pass through them freely. TRAP: Assuming the frames acted as solid walls caused wasted time planning around phantom obstacles.

GOAL: Guide the growing plug to the distant socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move and rotate the plug; special keys trigger teleportation. RULE: The plug consumes obstacles in its path, clearing the way as it expands. TRAP: Assuming obstacles block movement permanently; they vanish when the plug grows over them.

ESTABLISHED: The home is at (1,3). The card 3 program moves the piece down 3 cells to (4,3). FAILED: Assuming the plug size changes with the card 3 program, as it remains 1 cell in the demo but 2 in the panel. GOAL IS NOT: A simple coordinate match, as the demo's plug size contradicts the current board state. CONTROLS: The card 3 program executes a downward move, shifting the piece's position without altering its dimensions.

GOAL: Navigate a grid to reach the exit box within a strict action limit while managing a depleting health bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step per press; no sliding or dash mechanics are available. RULE: The health bar decreases with every action, forcing you to prioritize the shortest path and avoid backtracking. TRAP: Assuming you can survive multiple wrong moves; one extra step often triggers an automatic reset and life loss.

ESTABLISHED: Touches register when the plus passes under a stationary block. No-op moves advance time and drain the bar. FAILED: Ignoring stationary collisions and skipping goal checks on blocked moves prevented finding a solution. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the coordinate; the specific shape orientation must match the glyph exactly upon arrival. CONTROLS: Movement shifts the plus. Blocked moves still tick. Verify shape changes live after every touch to confirm rotation logic.
